passages.2022-1: The main threat to maintaining progress in human development comes from the increasingly evident unsustainability of production and consumption patterns. Current production models rely heavily on fossil fuels. We now know that this is unsustainable because the resources are finite. The close link between economic growth and greenhouse gas emissions needs to be severed for human development to become truly sustainable. Some developed countries have begun to alleviate the worst effects by expanding recycling and investing in public transport and infrastructure. But most developing countries are hampered by the high costs and low availability of clean energy sources. Developed countries need to support developing countries’ transition to sustainable human development.
passages.2022-3: Unless the forces and tendencies which are responsible for destroying the country’s environment are checked in the near future and afforestation of denuded areas is taken up on a massive scale, the harshness of the climatic conditions and soil erosion by wind and water will increase to such an extent that agriculture, which is the mainstay of our people, will gradually become impossible. The desert countries of the world and our own desert areas in Rajasthan are a grim reminder of the consequences of large-scale deforestation. Pockets of desert-like landscape are now appearing in other parts of the country including the Sutlej-Ganga Plains and the Deccan Plateau. Where only a few decades back there used to be lush green forests with perennial streams and springs, there is only brown earth, bare of vegetation, without any water in the streams and springs except in the rainy season.
passages.2022-11: “In simple matters like shoe-making, we think only a specially trained person will serve our purpose, but in politics, we presume that everyone who knows how to get votes knows how to administer a State. When we are ill, we call for a trained physician, whose degree is a guarantee of specific preparation and technical competence—we do not ask for the handsomest physician, or the most eloquent one: well then, when the whole State is ill should we not look for the service and guidance of the wisest and the best?”
passages.2022-12: The poverty line is quite unsatisfactory when it comes to grasping the extent of poverty in India. It is not only because of its extremely narrow definition of ‘who is poor’ and the debatable methodology used to count the poor, but also because of a more fundamental assumption underlying it. It exclusively relies on the notion of poverty as insufficient income or insufficient purchasing power. One can better categorize it by calling it income poverty. If poverty is ultimately about deprivations affecting human well-being, then income poverty is only one aspect of it. Poverty of a life, in our view, lies not merely in the impoverished state in which the person actually lives, but also in the lack of real opportunity given by social constraints as well as personal circumstances—to choose other types of living. Even the relevance of low incomes, meagre possessions, and other aspects of what are standardly seen as economic poverty relate ultimately to their role in curtailing capabilities, i.e., their role in severely restricting the choices people have to lead variable and valued lives.
passages.2022-21: In some places in the world, the productivity of staples such as rice and wheat has reached a plateau. Neither new strains nor fancy agrochemicals are raising the yields. Nor is there much unfarmed land left that is suitable to be brought under the plough. If global temperature continues to rise, some places will become unsuitable for farming. Application of technology can help overcome these problems. Agricultural technology is changing fast. Much of this change is brought about by affluent farmers in the West/Americas. Techniques developed in the West are being adapted in some places to make tropical crops more productive. Technology is of little use if it is not adapted. In the developing world, that applies as much to existing farming techniques as it does to the latest advances in genetic modification. Extending to the smallholders and subsistence farmers of Africa and Asia the best of today’s agricultural practices, in such simple matters as how much fertilizers to apply and when, would lead to a greatly increased availability of food for humanity. So would things like better roads and storage facilities, to allow for the carriage of surpluses to markets and reduce wastage.
passages.2022-31: Natural selection cannot anticipate future environments on the earth. Therefore, the set of existing organisms can never be fully prepared for environmental catastrophes that await life. An outcome of this is the extinction of those species which cannot overcome environmental adversity. This failure to survive, in modern terms, can be attributed to the genomes which are unable to withstand geological vagaries or biological mishaps (infections, diseases and so on). In biological evolution on the earth, extinction of species has been a major feature. The earth may presently have up to ten million species, yet more than 90% of species that have ever lived on the earth are now extinct. Once again, the creationist doctrines fail to satisfactorily address why a divine creator will firstly bother to create millions of species and then allow them to perish. The Darwinian explanation for extinct life is once again simple, elegant and at once convincing—organisms go extinct as a function of environmental or biological assaults for which their inheritance deems them ill-equipped. Therefore, the so-called Darwinian theory of evolution is not a theory at all. Evolution happens—this is a fact. The mechanism of evolution (Darwin proposed natural selection) is amply supported by scientific data. Indeed, to date no single zoological, botanical, geological, paleontological, genetic or physical evidence has refuted either of the central two main Darwinian ideas. If religion is not taken into consideration, Darwinian laws are acceptable just like the laws proposed by Copernicus, Galileo, Newton and Einstein—sets of natural laws that explain natural phenomena in the universe.
passages.2022-34: With steady economic growth, higher literacy and increasing skill levels, the number of Indian middle- class families has gone up exponentially. Direct results of the affluence have been changes in dietary patterns and energy consumption levels. People have moved to a higher protein-based diet like milk products, fish and meat, all of which need significantly more water to produce than cereal-based diets. Increasing use of electronic and electric machines/gadgets and motor vehicles needs more and more energy and generation of energy needs water.
passages.2022-41: For two or three generations past, ever-increasing numbers of individuals have been living as workers merely, not as human beings. An excessive amount of labour is rule today in every circle of society, with the result that man’s spiritual element cannot thrive. He finds it very difficult to spend his little leisure in serious activities. He does not want to think; or he cannot even if he wants to. He seeks not self- improvement, but entertainment which would enable him to be mentally idle and to forget his usual activities. Therefore, the so-called culture of our age is dependant more on cinema than on theatre, more on newspapers, magazines and crime stories than on serious literature.
passages.2022-43: The demographic dividend, which has begun in India and is expected to last another few decades, is a great window of opportunity. The demographic dividend is basically a swelling in the working age population, which conversely means that the relative ratio of very young and very old will, for a while, be on the decline. From the experience of Ireland and China, we know that this can be a source of energy and an engine of economic growth. The demographic dividend tends to raise a nation’s savings rate since in any nation, it is the working age population that is the main saver. And since the savings rate is an important driver of growth, this should help elevate our growth rate. However, the benefits of demographic dividend depend on the quality of the working age population. And this implies bringing back the importance of education, acquisition of skills and human capital.
passages.2022-51: In an economic organization, allowing mankind to benefit by the productivity of machines should lead to a very good life of leisure, and much leisure is apt to be tedious except to those who have intelligent activities and interests. If a leisured population is to be happy, it must be an educated population, and must be educated with a view to enjoyment as well as to the direct usefulness of technical knowledge.
passages.2022-52: If presents bring less thrill now that we are grown up, perhaps it is because we have too much already; or perhaps it is because we have lost the fullness of the joy of giving, and with it the fullness of the joy of receiving. Children’s fears are poignant, their miseries are acute, but they do not look too forward nor too far backward. Their joys are clear and complete, because they have not yet learnt always to add ‘but’ to every proposition. Perhaps we are too cautious, too anxious, too sceptical. Perhaps some of our cares would shrink if we thought less about them and entered with more single-minded enjoyment into the happiness that come our way.
passages.2022-61: The majority of people who fail to accumulate money sufficient for their needs, are generally, easily influenced by the opinions of others. They permit the newspapers and the gossiping neighbours to do their thinking for them. Opinions are the cheapest commodities on the earth. Everyone has a flock of opinions ready to be wished upon by anyone who will accept them. If you are influenced by opinions when you reach decisions, you will not succeed in any undertaking.
passages.2022-63: “The social order is a sacred right which is the basis of all other rights. Nevertheless, this right does not come from nature, and must therefore be founded on conventions.”
passages.2022-71: To encourage research is one of the functions of a university. Contemporary universities have encouraged research, not only in those cases where research is necessary, but on all sorts of entirely unprofitable subjects as well. Scientific research is probably never completely valueless. However silly and insignificant it may seem, however mechanical and unintelligent the labours of the researchers, there is always a chance that the results may be of value to the investigator of talent, who can use the facts collected for him by uninspired but industrious researchers as the basis of some fruitful generalization. But where research is not original, but consists in the mere rearrangement of existing materials, where its object is not scientific but literary or historical, then there is a risk of the whole business becoming merely futile.
passages.2022-73: How best can the problems of floods and droughts be addressed so that the losses are minimal and the system becomes resilient? In this context, one important point that needs to be noted is that India gets ‘too much’ water (about 75% of annual precipitation) during 120 days (June to September) and ‘too little’ for the remaining 245 days. This skewed water availability has to be managed and regulated for its consumption throughout the year.

questions.q:
Unsustainability in production pattern is due to which of the following?
1. Heavy dependence on fossil fuels
2. Limited availability of resources
3. Expansion of recycling
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Production relies on fossil fuels, which is unsustainable because resources are finite (1, 2). Recycling is mentioned only as a remedy, not a cause.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: Developed countries can support developing countries’ transition to sustainable human development by
1. making clean energy sources available at low cost
2. providing loans for improving their public transport at nominal interest rates
3. encouraging them to change their production and consumption patterns
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The passage names high cost and low availability of clean energy as barriers and cites public transport and infrastructure as helpful steps. Cheap clean energy and low-cost loans for transport address these (1, 2); mere encouragement does not.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q2

questions.q:
According to the passage given above, deforestation and denudation will ultimately lead to which of the following?
1. Depletion of soil resource
2. Shortage of land for the common man
3. Lack of water for cultivation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The passage predicts soil erosion and land without water in streams and springs outside the rains — loss of soil (1) and water (3). Shortage of land for people is not mentioned.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q3

questions.q: What is the value of X in the sequence 20, 10, 10, 15, 30, 75, X?
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q4

questions.q: An Identity Card has the number ABCDEFG, not necessarily in that order, where each letter represents a distinct digit (1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 only). The number is divisible by 9. After deleting the first digit from the right, the resulting number is divisible by 6. After deleting two digits from the right of original number, the resulting number is divisible by 5. After deleting three digits from the right of original number, the resulting number is divisible by 4. After deleting four digits from the right of original number, the resulting number is divisible by 3. After deleting five digits from the right of original number, the resulting number is divisible by 2. Which of the following is a possible value for the sum of the middle three digits of the number?
questions.e: Divisibility rules, applied from the left, force the last digit G = 9, E = 5 (divisible by 5), and the even digits 2, 4, 8 into B, D, F; the 3 and 4 tests then fix B = 4 and D = 2. The middle three C + D + E come to 8 among the options.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q5

questions.q: Two friends X and Y start running and they run together for 50 m in the same direction and reach a point. X turns right and runs 60 m, while Y turns left and runs 40 m. Then X turns left and runs 50 m and stops, while Y turns right and runs 50 m and then stops. How far are the two friends from each other now?
questions.e: After the first turns X and Y head in opposite directions, ending 60 + 40 = 100 m apart. Their next turns both point the same way for 50 m, so the gap stays 100 m.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q6

questions.q: Which date of June 2099 among the following is Sunday?
questions.e: 31 December 2098 is a Wednesday; January–May 2099 add 151 days = 4 odd days, making 31 May a Sunday. So 7 June 2099 is a Sunday.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q7

questions.q:
A bill for ₹1,840 is paid in the denominations of ₹50, ₹20 and ₹10 notes. 50 notes in all are used. Consider the following statements:
1. 25 notes of ₹50 are used and the remaining are in the denominations of ₹20 and ₹10.
2. 35 notes of ₹20 are used and the remaining are in the denominations of ₹50 and ₹10.
3. 20 notes of ₹10 are used and the remaining are in the denominations of ₹50 and ₹20.
Which of the above statements are not correct?
questions.e: With a, b, c notes of ₹50, ₹20, ₹10: a + b + c = 50 and 5a + 2b + c = 184, so 4a + b = 134. a = 25 gives c = −9; b = 35 gives a non-integer a; c = 20 gives a = 104/3. None works, so all three are incorrect.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q8

questions.q: Which number amongst 2⁴⁰, 3²¹, 4¹⁸ and 8¹² is the smallest?
questions.e: 4¹⁸ = 2³⁶ and 8¹² = 2³⁶, both below 2⁴⁰. 3²¹ = (3⁷)³ = 2187³, while 2³⁶ = (2¹²)³ = 4096³. So 3²¹ is smallest.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q9

questions.q: The digits 1 to 9 are arranged in three rows in such a way that each row contains three digits, and the number formed in the second row is twice the number formed in the first row; and the number formed in the third row is thrice the number formed in the first row. Repetition of digits is not allowed. If only three of the four digits 2, 3, 7 and 9 are allowed to use in the first row, how many such combinations are possible to be arranged in the three rows?
questions.e: The first row N must keep 3N under 1000 and use three of 2, 3, 7, 9. Checking, only 273 (546, 819) and 327 (654, 981) use all nine digits once: 2.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q10

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the message of the author of the passage?
o: We assume that in a democracy, any politician is qualified to administer a State.
Politicians should be selected from those trained in administration.
We need to devise a method of barring incompetence from public office.
As voters select their administrators, the eligibility of politicians to administer a State cannot be questioned.
questions.e: We insist on trained shoe-makers and doctors yet accept anyone who wins votes to run the State, and the author asks for the wisest and best. Incompetence must be barred from public office — (c).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q11

questions.q: Why is the methodology adopted in India to count the ‘poor’ debatable?
o: There is some confusion regarding what should constitute the ‘poverty line’.
There are wide diversities in the condition of the rural and urban poor.
There is no uniform global standard for measuring income poverty.
It is based on the proposition of poverty as meagre income or buying capacity.
questions.e: The count of the poor relies only on income or purchasing power, which the author calls too narrow — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q12

questions.q: Why is income poverty only one measure of counting the ‘poor’?
o: It talks of only one kind of deprivation ignoring all others.
Other deprivations in a human life have nothing to do with lack of purchasing power.
Income poverty is not a permanent condition, it changes from time to time.
Income poverty restricts human choices only at a point of time.
questions.e: Poverty covers all deprivations that affect well-being; income is only one of them — (a).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q13

questions.q: What does the author mean by ‘poverty of a life’?
o: All deprivations in a human life which stem not only from lack of income but lack of real opportunities
Impoverished state of poor people in rural and urban areas
Missed opportunities in diverse personal circumstances
Material as well as non-material deprivations in a human life which restrict human choices permanently
questions.e: Poverty of a life lies in both the impoverished state and the lack of real opportunity to live otherwise — deprivation from lack of income and of real opportunities (a).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q14

questions.q: X and Y run a 3 km race along a circular course of length 300 m. Their speeds are in the ratio 3:2. If they start together in the same direction, how many times would the first one pass the other (the start-off is not counted as passing)?
questions.e: When X finishes 3000 m, Y has run 2000 m; X gains 1000 m, which is 3 full laps of 300 m (plus 100 m). Three passes.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q15

questions.q: If the order of the letters in the English alphabet is reversed and each letter represents the letter whose position it occupies, then which one of the following represents ‘LUCKNOW’?
questions.e: Reversed, each letter maps to the one whose position adds with it to 27: L→O, U→F, C→X, K→P, N→M, O→L, W→D: OFXPMLD.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q16

questions.q: In a tournament of Chess having 150 entrants, a player is eliminated whenever he loses a match. It is given that no match results in a tie/draw. How many matches are played in the entire tournament?
questions.e: Every match eliminates one player, and 149 must be eliminated to leave a winner: 149 matches.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q17

questions.q: How many 3-digit natural numbers (without repetition of digits) are there such that each digit is odd and the number is divisible by 5?
questions.e: Divisible by 5 with odd digits means ending in 5. The first two places from 1, 3, 7, 9 without repetition: 4 × 3 = 12.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q18

questions.q:
Consider the Question and two Statements given below:
Question: Is x an integer?
Statement–1: x/3 is not an integer.
Statement–2: 3x is an integer.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the Question and the Statements?
o: Statement–1 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Statement–2 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are not sufficient to answer the Question
questions.e: x = 1 and x = 1/3 satisfy both statements, but only one is an integer. Not sufficient together.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q19

questions.q: The increase in the price of a certain item was 25%. Then the price was decreased by 20% and then again increased by 10%. What is the resultant increase in the price?
questions.e: 1.25 × 0.8 = 1, so the first two changes cancel; the final 10% rise remains.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q20

questions.q:
Based on the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
1. Development of agricultural technology is confined to developed countries.
2. Agricultural technology is not adapted in developing countries.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Change comes 'much' (not all) from affluent Western farmers, and Western techniques are being adapted in some places. Both assumptions contradict or overstate the passage.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q21

questions.q:
Based on the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
1. Poor countries need to bring about change in their existing farming techniques.
2. Developed countries have better infrastructure and they waste less food.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Technology must be adapted, and in the developing world that applies to existing farming techniques too — so poor countries must change how they farm (1). Infrastructure and food waste are not compared.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q22

questions.q:
Based on the above passage, the following assumptions have been made:
1. Growing enough food for future generations will be a challenge.
2. Corporate farming is a viable option for food security in poor countries.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Plateauing yields, little spare land and rising heat assume feeding future generations will be hard (1). Corporate farming is never mentioned.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q23

questions.q: The letters A, B, C, D and E are arranged in such a way that there are exactly two letters between A and E. How many such arrangements are possible?
questions.e: A and E occupy places 1 & 4 or 2 & 5, in either order: 4 ways. The other three letters: 3! = 6. Total 24.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q24

questions.q:
Consider the Question and two Statements given below:
Question: Is Z brother of X?
Statement–1: X is a brother of Y and Y is a brother of Z.
Statement–2: X, Y and Z are siblings.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the Question and the Statements?
o: Statement–1 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Statement–2 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are not sufficient to answer the Question
questions.e: The statements show X, Y and Z are siblings and X, Y male, but Z's sex is unknown. Not sufficient even together.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q25

questions.q: On one side of a 1.01 km long road, 101 plants are planted at equal distance from each other. What is the total distance between 5 consecutive plants?
questions.e: 101 plants make 100 gaps over 1010 m: 10.1 m each. Five consecutive plants span 4 gaps: 40.4 m.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q26

questions.q: A, B and C are three places such that there are three different roads from A to B, four different roads from B to C and three different roads from A to C. In how many different ways can one travel from A to C using these roads?
questions.e: Direct A→C: 3 ways; via B: 3 × 4 = 12. Total 15.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q27

questions.q: A has some coins. He gives half of the coins and 2 more to B. B gives half of the coins and 2 more to C. C gives half of the coins and 2 more to D. The number of coins D has now, is the smallest two-digit number. How many coins does A have in the beginning?
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q28

questions.q: In the series AABABCABCDABCDE..., which letter appears at the 100th place?
questions.e: Blocks A, AB, ABC … of lengths 1, 2, 3 …; 13 blocks fill 91 places. The 100th is the 9th letter of block 14: I.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q29

questions.q: Three persons A, B and C are standing in a queue not necessarily in the same order. There are 4 persons between A and B, and 7 persons between B and C. If there are 11 persons ahead of C and 13 behind A, what could be the minimum number of persons in the queue?
questions.e: C is 12th, so B is 4th or 20th and A is 9th, 15th or 25th. With 13 behind A, the queue is smallest when A is 9th: 9 + 13 = 22.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q30

questions.q:
According to the passage, natural selection cannot anticipate future environments on the earth as
1. species not fully prepared to face the environmental changes that await them will face extinction
2. all the existing species would get extinct as their genomes will not withstand biological mishaps
3. inability of the genome to withstand environmental changes would result in extinction
4. extinction of species is a common feature
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Unprepared species go extinct (1), because genomes cannot withstand environmental or biological shocks (3), and extinction has been a major feature of life (4). The passage does not say all species will die out.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q31

questions.q: The passage suggests that Darwinian theory of evolution is not a theory at all because
o: it does not satisfy the creationist doctrine
extinction is a function of environment and biological assaults
there are no evidences to refute it
existence of organisms is attributed to a creator
questions.e: The author treats evolution as fact because extinction is simply explained as a result of environmental and biological assaults — (b).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q32

questions.q:
With reference to the passage, the following assumptions have been made:
1. Only species that have the ability to overcome environmental catastrophes will survive and perpetuate.
2. More than 90% of the species on the earth are in the danger of getting extinct due to drastic changes in the environment.
3. Darwin’s theory explains all the natural phenomena.
Which of the above assumptions is/are valid?
questions.e: Only species able to overcome catastrophes survive (1). The 90% figure refers to past species, and the passage never says Darwin explains all phenomena.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q33

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best reflects the crux of the passage?
o: People should be persuaded to continue with the mainly Indian traditional cereal-based diets.
India needs to focus on developing agricultural productivity and capacity for more energy generation in the coming years.
Modern technological developments result in the change of cultural and social behaviour of the people.
Water management practices in India need to change dramatically in the coming years.
questions.e: Richer diets and more gadgets and vehicles all raise water demand, directly or through energy. Water management must change dramatically — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q34

questions.q: How many seconds in total are there in x weeks, x days, x hours, x minutes and x seconds?
questions.e: Week 604800 s + day 86400 + hour 3600 + minute 60 + second 1 = 694861 s per x.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q35

questions.q: P, Q, R, S, T and U are six members of a family. R is the spouse of Q. U is the mother of T and S is the daughter of U. P’s daughter is T and R’s son is P. There are two couples in the family. Which one of the following is correct?
o: Q is the grandfather of T
Q is the grandmother of T
R is the mother of P
T is the granddaughter of Q
questions.e: UPSC dropped this item. Q and R are P's parents and P and U are T's parents, so T is Q's granddaughter; Q's and R's genders are never given.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q36

questions.q:
Consider the Question and two Statements given below in respect of three cities P, Q and R in a State:
Question: How far is city P from city Q?
Statement–1: City Q is 18 km from city R.
Statement–2: City P is 43 km from city R.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the Question and the Statements?
o: Statement–1 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Statement–2 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are not sufficient to answer the Question
questions.e: Distances RP = 43 and RQ = 18 fix PQ only with directions; PQ can be anywhere from 25 to 61 km. Not sufficient.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q37

questions.q:
Two Statements followed by four Conclusions are given below. You have to take the Statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from the commonly known facts. Read all the Conclusions and then decide which of the given Conclusions logically follows/follow from the Statements, disregarding the commonly known facts:
Statement–1: All pens are books.
Statement–2: No chair is a pen.
Conclusion–I: All chairs are books.
Conclusion–II: Some chairs are pens.
Conclusion–III: All books are chairs.
Conclusion–IV: No chair is a book.
Which one of the following is correct?
questions.e: 'All pens are books' and 'No chair is a pen' fix nothing about chairs and books. I and IV are only possible, II contradicts the statements, III is not implied. None follows.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q38

questions.q:
Three Statements followed by three Conclusions are given below. You have to take the Statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from the commonly known facts. Read all the Conclusions and then decide which of the given Conclusions logically follows/follow from the Statements, disregarding the commonly known facts:
Statement–1: Some doctors are teachers.
Statement–2: All teachers are engineers.
Statement–3: All engineers are scientists.
Conclusion–I: Some scientists are doctors.
Conclusion–II: All engineers are doctors.
Conclusion–III: Some engineers are doctors.
Which one of the following is correct?
questions.e: Doctors who are teachers are engineers and scientists, so some engineers and some scientists are doctors (I, III). 'All engineers are doctors' does not follow.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q39

questions.q: Eight students A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit around a circular table, equidistant from each other, facing the centre of the table, not necessarily in the same order. B and D sit neither adjacent to C nor opposite to C. A sits in between E and D, and F sits in between B and H. Which one of the following is definitely correct?
o: B sits in between A and G
questions.e: More than one seating fits the conditions; in some C faces G, in others E faces F, and B is never beside A. None of (a)–(c) is definite.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q40

questions.q: The passage is based on the idea that
o: the great evil of our age is overstrain
man cannot care for his spiritual welfare
questions.e: Excess labour is blamed for a stunted inner life and a taste for idle amusement. The underlying idea: overstrain is the great evil of the age — (b).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q41

questions.q: Man does not seek self-improvement because he
o: has no time to do so
loves amusement and is mentally idle
questions.e: The passage says he seeks not self-improvement but entertainment that lets him be mentally idle — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q42

questions.q:
Which of the following would invariably happen in a country, when the demographic dividend has begun to operate?
1. The number of illiterate people will decrease.
2. The ratio of very old and very young will decrease for a while.
3. Population growth rate will quickly stabilize.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The passage defines the dividend as the ratio of very young and very old declining for a while (2). Literacy and population growth are not automatic results.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q43

questions.q:
With reference to the passage, which of the following inferences can be drawn?
1. Demographic dividend is an essential condition for a country to rapidly increase its economic growth rate.
2. Promotion of higher education is an essential condition for a country for its rapid economic growth.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The dividend can help growth, and benefits depend on education and skills, but neither is called an essential condition, and higher education is not singled out. Neither.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q44

questions.q:
Five friends P, Q, X, Y and Z purchased some notebooks. The relevant information is given below:
1. Z purchased 8 notebooks more than X did.
2. P and Q together purchased 21 notebooks.
3. Q purchased 5 notebooks less than P did.
4. X and Y together purchased 28 notebooks.
5. P purchased 5 notebooks more than X did. If each notebook is priced ₹40, then what is the total cost of all the notebooks?
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q45

questions.q: A man started from home at 14:30 hours and drove to village, arriving there when the village clock indicated 15:15 hours. After staying for 25 minutes, he drove back by a different route of length 1.25 times the first route at a rate twice as fast reaching home at 16:00 hours. As compared to the clock at home, the village clock is
questions.e: Away 90 minutes by home time, 65 of them driving. Return takes 1.25/2 = 0.625 of the outward time, so 1.625t = 65, t = 40. He reached the village at 15:10 home time; the village clock shows 15:15 — 5 minutes fast.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q46

questions.q:
A person X wants to distribute some pens among six children A, B, C, D, E and F. Suppose A gets twice the number of pens received by B, three times that of C, four times that of D, five times that of E and six times that of
F. What is the minimum number of pens X should buy so that the number of pens each one gets is an even number?
questions.e: If A gets k, others get k/2 … k/6, all even, so k is a multiple of 4, 6, 8, 10, 12: k = 120. Total 120 + 60 + 40 + 30 + 24 + 20 = 294.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q47

questions.q:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting equidistant from each other around a circular table (facing the centre of the table).
Consider the Question and two Statements given below:
Question: Who is sitting on the immediate left of A?
Statement–1: B is sitting opposite to C and D is sitting opposite to E.
Statement–2: F is sitting on the immediate left of B.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the Question and the Statements?
o: Statement–1 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Statement–2 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are not sufficient to answer the Question
questions.e: Together the statements place F opposite A and fix A's right-hand neighbour, but A's left seat could be D or E. Not sufficient.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q48

questions.q:
Consider the Question and two Statements given below:
Question: What is the age of Manisha?
Statement–1: Manisha is 24 years younger than her mother.
Statement–2: 5 years later, the ages of Manisha and her mother will be in the ratio 3:5.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the Question and the Statements?
o: Statement–1 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Statement–2 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are not sufficient to answer the Question
questions.e: Mother = M + 24 and (M + 5)/(M + 29) = 3/5 gives M = 31. Both statements are needed.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q49

questions.q:
Six lectures A, B, C, D, E and F, each of one hour duration, are scheduled between 8:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.
Consider the Question and two Statements given below:
Question: Which lecture is in the third period?
Statement–1: Lecture F is preceded by A and followed by C.
Statement–2: There is no lecture after lecture B.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the Question and the Statements?
o: Statement–1 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Statement–2 alone is sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are sufficient to answer the Question
Both Statement–1 and Statement–2 are not sufficient to answer the Question
questions.e: B is last, but the block A-F-C can sit in periods 1–3, 2–4 or 3–5, so period 3 is not fixed. Not sufficient.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q50

questions.q: Which of the following statements best reflects the underlying tone of the passage?
o: Only an educated population can best make use of the benefits of economic progress.
All economic development should be aimed at the creation of leisure.
An increase in the educated population of a country leads to an increase in the happiness of its people.
Use of machines should be encouraged in order to create a large leisured population.
questions.e: Machines can create leisure, but leisure is tedious unless people have intelligent interests; a leisured people is happy only if educated — (a).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q51

questions.q: With reference to the passage, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It is not possible for adults to feel thrilled by presents.
There can be more than one reason why adults feel less thrilled by presents.
The author does not know why adults feel less thrilled by presents.
Adults have less capacity to feel the joy of loving or being loved.
questions.e: The author gives two possible reasons with 'perhaps … or perhaps', so there can be more than one reason — (b).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q52

questions.q: The author of the passage is against
o: worrying too much about the past and future
being in the habit of thinking about presents
not being thrilled by new things
giving and receiving joy only partially
questions.e: Children's joys are full because they look neither far ahead nor far back, and our cares would shrink if we thought less about them. He is against worrying about past and future — (a).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q53

questions.q:
Let A, B and C represent distinct non-zero digits. Suppose x is the sum of all possible 3-digit numbers formed by A, B and C without repetition.
Consider the following statements:
1. The 4-digit least value of x is 1332.
2. The 3-digit greatest value of x is 888.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: The six numbers sum to 222 × (A + B + C). The least digit sum is 6, so the least x is 1332 (1 true), and x is never a 3-digit number (2 false).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q54

questions.q: There is a numeric lock which has a 3-digit PIN. The PIN contains digits 1 to 7. There is no repetition of digits. The digits in the PIN from left to right are in decreasing order. Any two digits in the PIN differ by at least 2. How many maximum attempts does one need to find out the PIN with certainty?
questions.e: Choose three digits from 1–7 pairwise at least 2 apart; each set gives one decreasing PIN. Such sets number C(5, 3) = 10.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q55

questions.q: There are eight equidistant points on a circle. How many right-angled triangles can be drawn using these points as vertices and taking the diameter as one side of the triangle?
questions.e: 8 points give 4 diameters; each with any of the other 6 points forms a right angle in a semicircle: 24.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q56

questions.q: 24 men and 12 women can do a piece of work in 30 days. In how many days can 12 men and 24 women do the same piece of work?
o: Less than 30 days or more than 30 days
Data is inadequate to draw any conclusion
questions.e: The answer depends on how men's and women's rates compare, which is not given. Data inadequate.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q57

questions.q: What is the remainder when 91 × 92 × 93 × 94 × 95 × 96 × 97 × 98 × 99 is divided by 1261?
questions.e: 1261 = 13 × 97. The product contains 91 = 7 × 13 and 97, so it is divisible by 1261: remainder 0.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q58

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of a rectangular sheet of length 20 cm and breadth 8 cm:
1. It is possible to cut the sheet exactly into 4 square sheets.
2. It is possible to cut the sheet into 10 triangular sheets of equal area.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: Two 8 × 8 and two 4 × 4 squares exactly fill 20 × 8, and five 4 × 8 strips cut diagonally give 10 equal triangles. Both.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q59

questions.q: When 70% of a number x is added to another number y, the sum becomes 165% of the value of y. When 60% of the number x is added to another number z, then the sum becomes 165% of the value of z. Which one of the following is correct?
questions.e: 0.7x = 0.65y gives y = 14x/13; 0.6x = 0.65z gives z = 12x/13. So z < x < y.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q60

questions.q: Which one of the following is implied by the passage?
o: Most of the people do not accumulate money for their needs.
Most of the people never fail to accumulate money for their needs.
There are people who fail to accumulate money for their needs.
There is no need to accumulate money.
questions.e: The passage opens by speaking of 'the majority of people who fail to accumulate money', taking for granted that such people exist — (c).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q61

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: People should not be influenced by the opinions of others.
People should accumulate as much money as they can.
People should neither give nor accept the opinions.
People will succeed in any undertaking if they do not accept any opinion at all.
questions.e: Failure is linked to being swayed by others' opinions, and anyone so swayed 'will not succeed'. Main idea: do not be influenced by others' opinions — (a).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q62

questions.q:
With reference to the above passage, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Conventions are the sources of rights of man.
2. Rights of man can be exercised only when there is a social order.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: All rights rest on the social order, which rests on conventions, so conventions are the source of rights (1), and rights exist only where there is a social order (2). Both.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q63

questions.q: Two candidates X and Y contested an election. 80% of voters cast their vote and there were no invalid votes. There was no NOTA (None of the above) option. X got 56% of the votes cast and won by 1440 votes. What is the total number of voters in the voters list?
questions.e: X 56%, Y 44% of votes cast: the margin 12% = 1440, so votes cast = 12000 = 80% of voters. Voters = 15000.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q64

questions.q: What is the smallest number greater than 1000 that when divided by any one of the numbers 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 leaves a remainder of 3?
questions.e: LCM(6, 9, 12, 15, 18) = 180. The first multiple above 997 is 1080; add 3: 1083.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q65

questions.q: Let p be a two-digit number and q be the number consisting of same digits written in reverse order. If p × q = 2430, then what is the difference between p and q?
questions.e: 2430 = 45 × 54, a number and its reverse. Difference 9.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q66

questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of two natural numbers p and q such that p is a prime number and q is a composite number:
1. p × q can be an odd number.
2. q/p can be a prime number.
3. p + q can be a prime number.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Examples suffice: 3 × 9 = 27 is odd; 6 ÷ 2 = 3 is prime; 2 + 9 = 11 is prime. All three can be true.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q67

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Between 3:16 p.m. and 3:17 p.m., both hour hand and minute hand coincide.
2. Between 4:58 p.m. and 4:59 p.m., both minute hand and second hand coincide.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: Hour and minute hands meet 16 4/11 minutes after 3. After 4:58 the second hand meets the minute hand about 59 seconds later, before 4:59. Both.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q68

questions.q: There are two containers X and Y. X contains 100 ml of milk and Y contains 100 ml of water. 20 ml of milk from X is transferred to Y. After mixing well, 20 ml of the mixture in Y is transferred back to X. If m denotes the proportion of milk in X and n denotes the proportion of water in Y, then which one of the following is correct?
o: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data
questions.e: Both containers end at 100 ml, so the water moved into X equals the milk left in Y. X's milk share equals Y's water share: m = n.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q69

questions.q: A pie chart gives the expenditure on five different items A, B, C, D and E in a household. If B, C, D and E correspond to 90°, 50°, 45° and 75° respectively, then what is the percentage of expenditure on item A?
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q70

questions.q: The author’s assumption about scientific research is that
o: it is never without some value
questions.e: The author says scientific research is 'probably never completely valueless' — it is never without some value (c), not always very valuable.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q71

questions.q: According to the author
o: not many research results can be of value to an intelligent investigator
a research result is always valuable to an intelligent investigator
any research result can be of value to an intelligent investigator
a research result must always be of some value to an intelligent investigator
questions.e: 'There is always a chance that the results may be of value' to a talented investigator — any result can be of value (c), though none is guaranteed.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q72

questions.q: Which one of the following best reflects the practical, rational and lasting solution?
o: Constructing huge concrete storage tanks and canals across the country
Changing the cropping patterns and farming practices
Interlinking of rivers across the country
Buffer stocking of water through dams and recharging aquifers
questions.e: Rain falls mostly in about 120 days and little in the rest of the year. Storing monsoon water in dams and aquifers for year-round use is the lasting fix — (d).
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q73

questions.q: If 15 × 14 × 13 × ··· × 3 × 2 × 1 = 3ᵐ × n, where m and n are positive integers, then what is the maximum value of m?
questions.e: Powers of 3 in 15!: multiples of 3 (3, 6, 9, 12, 15) give 5, and 9 gives one more: m = 6.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q74

questions.q: What is the value of X in the sequence 2, 12, 36, 80, 150, X?
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q75

questions.q: One non-zero digit, one vowel and one consonant from English alphabet (in capital) are to be used in forming passwords, such that each password has to start with a vowel and end with a consonant. How many such passwords can be generated?
questions.e: Vowel first (5), digit in the middle (9), consonant last (21): 5 × 9 × 21 = 945.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q76

questions.q: There are 9 cups placed on a table arranged in equal number of rows and columns out of which 6 cups contain coffee and 3 cups contain tea. In how many ways can they be arranged so that each row should contain at least one cup of coffee?
questions.e: In a 3 × 3 grid choose 3 tea places: C(9, 3) = 84. Only the 3 choices filling a whole row break the rule: 81.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q77

questions.q: The sum of three consecutive integers is equal to their product. How many such possibilities are there?
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q78

questions.q: What is the number of numbers of the form 0·XY, where X and Y are distinct non-zero digits?
questions.e: X: 9 non-zero digits, Y: 8 others: 72.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q79

questions.q:
The average weight of A, B, C is 40 kg, the average weight of B, D, E is 42 kg and the weight of F is equal to that of
B. What is the average weight of A, B, C, D, E and F?
o: Cannot be determined as data is inadequate
questions.e: A + B + C = 120, B + D + E = 126 and F = B, so all six total 246: average 41 kg.
questions.s: UPSC Prelims 2022, CSAT Paper II, Q80
